deities: Lord Rama (originally intended; idol never installed)

history.period: 16th century (begun under Madhukar Shah, completed by Vir Singh Deo)
history.summary: Grand Bundela temple built by King Madhukar Shah for his Rama-devotee wife Rani Ganeshkuwari and completed by his son Vir Singh Deo (16th century, Akbar's reign), designed to enshrine the Rama idol brought from Ayodhya. Because the idol remained immovable in the queen's palace — which became the Ram Raja Temple (RELATED RECORD: seq 1813) — this temple instead received a Radha-Krishna image, worshipped to this day. Its 344-ft (105 m) vimana is among the tallest in India, and its architecture blends temple, fort and palace elements on a 4.5-m-high platform. Maintained by the ASI. Note: older sources list the district as Tikamgarh; Orchha moved to Niwari district (created 2018). Do NOT confuse with the Chaturbhuj temples of Maihar Fort (seq 1810), Khajuraho (c.1100 CE), or Gwalior Fort (c.875 CE).

name: Chaturbhuj Temple
town_description: Orchha is a historic town in Niwari district (older sources say Tikamgarh) on the Betwa river, founded in 1531 by Rudra Pratap Singh as the capital of the Bundela Rajputs. It holds the Orchha Fort complex, Jahangir Mahal and Rani Mahal palaces, the Ram Raja temple, and the famous riverfront cenotaphs (chhatris) of the Bundela rulers. It lies about 15 km from Jhansi in Uttar Pradesh, its main railhead.

travel.road: On SH-37/NH-39 network; regular buses and taxis from Jhansi, Gwalior and Bhopal

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; early morning or late afternoon for the rooftop views of the Betwa and Orchha town
